description: We are an energetic team of curious 5th-grade students! We are passionate about space, science, and coding. We love generating creative ideas and solving problems together. Anyone who wants to dream big and make a difference at NASA Space Apps can have an amazing adventure with us. To join our team, simply be curious, love researching, and be eager to create together!
summary:
We developed "Whispers from the Stars: The Forgotten Explorers," an interactive digital storytelling presentation and AI-voiced audio-visual story created by our team of five 5th-grade students.

To address the challenge of introducing school-age learners to NASA’s discarded off-world hardware, we transformed dense technical and historical mission data into an engaging, first-person narrative. Instead of listing dry facts, our project brings silent robotic explorers—specifically the Apollo 11 Eagle Lunar Module, the Opportunity Mars Rover, and the InSight Mars Lander—back to life. Using custom kid-friendly avatars, visual slides, and expressive AI voiceovers, each spacecraft shares its own journey, engineering design, and groundbreaking scientific discoveries, such as finding evidence of ancient liquid water and mapping Mars’s internal core.

This project matters because young students usually hear only about active space missions, missing the rich history that made today’s exploration possible. By building an emotional connection with these silent monuments on the Moon and Mars, our story inspires curiosity, makes space science accessible to kids, and ensures that humanity's robotic pioneers are abandoned in space, yet never forgotten.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?"Whispers from the Stars: The Forgotten Explorers" is an interactive, audio-visual digital storytelling project designed for school-age space enthusiasts. Instead of presenting dense technical text, our project brings three iconic NASA off-world machines—the Apollo 11 Eagle Lunar Module, the Opportunity (Oppy) Mars Rover, and the InSight Mars Lander—back to life through first-person narration. Users explore a structured visual slide presentation paired with expressive AI-generated character voices and custom kid-friendly avatars representing our 5th-grade team (Arya, Demir, Leon, Mihrali, and İnci). Each spacecraft introduces its mission, explains its engineering features, and shares the real scientific discoveries it made before going silent.

What are the benefits and intended impact? Young students mostly hear about active rockets and current missions, often overlooking the silent hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars. Our project bridges this gap by translating complex NASA mission data into an emotional, easy-to-understand story. Its intended impact is to spark scientific curiosity among elementary and middle school students, build empathy with robotic explorers, and show how past discoveries—like finding ancient water on Mars or measuring marsquakes—make future human spaceflight possible.

Tools, Software, and Hardware Used

  • Research & Structuring: Official NASA mission archives and NotebookLM to organize scientific facts and generate the educational slide structure.
  • Scriptwriting & AI Assistance: Gemini to translate complex astrophysical data into an engaging 5th-grade narrative and design custom team avatars.
  • Voiceover & Audio Production: AI Text-to-Speech (TTS) software to create distinct, expressive character voices for the Narrator, Eagle, Opportunity, and InSight.
  • Visual Presentation & Editing: Presentation and video editing tools (Canva / CapCut) to combine slides, subtitles, NASA imagery, and audio tracks on standard classroom laptops.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered What makes our project creative is turning silent, inanimate hardware into relatable storytellers with distinct personalities—from the historic pride of Eagle to the cheerful resilience of Oppy. As a team of five 5th-grade students, we carefully considered age-appropriateness, scientific accuracy, and accessibility. We ensured every date, location, and discovery (such as Oppy’s 15-year journey and InSight’s 1,300+ detected marsquakes) remained faithful to real NASA records while using clear language, visuals, and audio so learners of all backgrounds can easily enjoy and learn from the story.What does it do and how does it work?"Whispers from the Stars: The Forgotten Explorers" is an interactive, audio-visual digital storytelling project designed for school-age space enthusiasts.
